title: Layers of the Earth
examples: What is the difference between the mantle and the core?
How do scientists know about the layers deep inside Earth?
Can you explain what the seismic waves tell us?

explain.say: The Earth has several distinct layers, like an onion.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the layers of the Earth. Look at the crust, the upper mantle and the lower mantle. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The crust is the very thin, rocky layer we live on.
Below the crust is the mantle, which is very thick and hot.
Deepest is the core, which is made mostly of iron and nickel.
Seismic waves are vibrations that travel through the Earth.

items: P-waves: Travel through solids and liquids
draw.label: Wave Types

explain.say: These waves change speed and direction when they hit boundaries.

faq.q: How do scientists know about the core if they can't dig that deep?
faq.a: Scientists use instruments to detect waves that travel through the Earth. These waves change speed and direction when they hit different materials. This helps them map the layers.
asks: What evidence shows the core exists?
How do we study deep Earth layers?

faq.q: Is the mantle liquid or solid?
faq.a: The mantle is mostly solid rock, but it behaves like a very thick, flowing liquid over long periods. This movement is what causes plate tectonics.
asks: What is the state of the mantle rock?

faq.a: P-waves are primary waves that can travel through both solids and liquids. S-waves are secondary waves that can only travel through solid materials.
asks: Which wave type passes through liquid metal?

faq.a: The crust is the thinnest layer of the Earth. It is the outermost shell that we are standing on right now.
asks: Which layer is closest to the surface?

faq.q: Does the core generate the Earth's magnetic field?
faq.a: Yes, the movement of liquid metal in the outer core generates the Earth's magnetic field. This field protects us from solar radiation.
asks: Where does Earth's magnetosphere come from?
Is the liquid core responsible for the magnetic field?

facts: The Earth's crust is composed of continental and oceanic rock.
The mantle is the thick layer situated directly beneath the crust.
The core is composed mainly of iron and nickel metals.
S-waves cannot travel through liquid materials.

quiz.say: Which layer is primarily made of liquid iron and nickel?
quiz.show: Which layer is liquid iron and nickel?
quiz.why: The outer core is known to be liquid metal, which is key to generating the magnetic field.

wrong.0: The mantle is mostly solid rock, not liquid metal.
wrong.1: The inner core is solid, even though it is very hot.
wrong.3: The crust is solid rock, not liquid metal.

quiz.say: If seismic waves are detected passing through a material, what does the change in wave speed suggest?
quiz.show: Change in wave speed suggests what?

options.show: A change in the material's state or composition.
options.say: A change in the material's state or composition.

quiz.why: Different materials, like solid rock versus liquid metal, cause waves to travel at different speeds.

wrong.0: A change in speed does not mean the waves have stopped completely.
wrong.1: If the structure were uniform, the wave speed would remain constant.
wrong.2: The change in speed is a predictable scientific observation.

quiz.say: Which wave type can travel through both solid and liquid materials?
quiz.show: Which wave type passes through solids and liquids?
quiz.why: P-waves are the fastest waves and can pass through both solid and liquid states.

wrong.0: Surface waves are related to the ground, not the deep interior structure.
wrong.1: T-waves are not a recognized type of seismic wave.
wrong.3: S-waves are blocked by liquids because they need particles to shake.
